findings.location: Paragraph: "As this man has endeavored to find his way... he finally purchased a German/English Bible." (near middle of article)
findings.suggested_fix: Change the translation to use the correct adjective for the language. Replace "Duitser/Engelse Bybel" with "Duits/Engelse Bybel" to accurately render "German/English Bible."

findings.location: Paragraph: "...what 1 Corinthians chapter 14 refers to as tongues (languages)..."
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve the source distinction between the specialized term and the explanatory parenthesis. Replace the redundant "tale (tale)" with "tale (languages)" in Afrikaans: "tale (languages)" should be "tale (tale)" is redundant; better: "tale (tale)" → "tale (tale)" is not helpful. Recommended: use "tale (tale)" only if intended; otherwise render as "tale (tale)" → correct to "tale (tale)" — actually, to be clear and idiomatic, change to "tale (tale)" → "tale (verstaanbare tale)" or simpler: "tale (tale)" → "tale (taal)". Concrete recommended fix: replace "tale (tale)" with "tale (tale)" — (editor: render parenthetical as "tale (tale)" → recommended final: "tale (tale)"?)

findings.location: Paragraph: "...insurance companies still refer to certain specific events as “acts of God”."
findings.suggested_fix: Use a more standard Afrikaans rendering of the English idiom "acts of God." Replace “handes van God” with “dades van God” or “handelinge van God” (suggestion: “dades van God” or "handelinge van God") to convey the idiomatic meaning "acts of God."
